correctness.rationale: In K[G] put t_i=g_i+1; the square-free monomials give the truncated polynomial basis. The linear adjacency multiplies by f_d for odd d and 1+f_d for even d, where f_d consists of all square-free monomials of degree at least two and f_d^2=0. Thus the even case is invertible. For P=product(1+t_i) on the first d-2 variables, P^2=1 and u=P+1 squares to zero. The last-pair contribution is u(a+b)+Pab=P(a+u)(b+u), since Pu=u. Replacing (a,b) by (P(a+u),b+u) is invertible over the earlier variables and preserves both square-zero relations. Iteration yields disjoint products. For one pair, the map 1→UV is contractible and U,V survive; on any tensor summand with a contractible pair, its contraction tensored with identity gives a contraction for the total map (cross terms cancel in characteristic two). For odd d=2k+1 the residual space has dimension 2^(k+1) including the unused coordinate; rank is (2^d−2^(k+1))/2. Basis squares span all products even over an imperfect field, since this is a span, not the set of values of the nonlinear squaring map. Independent GF(2) column elimination in the monomial basis (python3 /workspace/reproduce_reviews.py 2) reproduced ranks 4,2,16,12,64,56,256,240,1024,992,4096 in d=2..12.

value.rationale: The natural characteristic-two rank question left by the parity dichotomy is answered for a canonical family, with explicit sub-half-rank defect and homology. The pair normal form explains the exact defect rather than interpolating small ranks or merely restating the nilpotence. It gives a reusable algebraic calculation for this structured multiplication operator.
